questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Senegal?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Senegal article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Senegal?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Senegal on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Senegal article.

questions.proof: The nation borders Mali in the east, Guinea-Bissau in the south, and Guinea in the south-east.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Senegal?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Senegal article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Senegal was given independence by France in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Senegal article.

questions.proof: Senegal was given independence by France in 1960.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This did not last long and Senegal and _____ broke apart into separate nations.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “broke”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Senegal article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: This did not last long and Senegal and Mali broke apart into separate nations.
